plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what others do. This ensures you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid (maximizing profit) and never overpay (never lose money) when you do win. Since payment equals the second-highest bid, not my own bid, there's no benefit to shading below value. I'll bid exactly my value of $31.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy, regardless of what other bidders do. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding my true value of $6 maximizes my expected profit without risk of overpaying. Bidding below value only reduces my chance of winning without improving my payoff conditional on winning.

My value for the item is $0. If I win, my earnings would be $0 minus the second-highest bid, which would result in a loss unless the second-highest bid is also $0. There's no incentive to bid anything above $0 since any positive bid risks a negative payoff if I win. The optimal strategy is to bid exactly $0 to avoid any potential loss while still complying with the auction rules.
